chapter_note: The chapter opens and closes with hagiographic dialogue frame, while the central teaching (¶2–¶6) gives a systematic correspondential exposition: daily solar rising/setting as the cosmic ‘first’ and ‘last’ moments (First Man’s descent/battle; Last Statue’s ascent/consummation). A clear late pastoral/application graft appears in ¶7 (direct address + imperative exhortation to preach/repent).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue attribution (‘Once again he speaks to his disciples’) and attention-command used as a frame, not cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: Two great mysteries are apparent in this shining sun, at its rising and setting. Now, at the moment when it rises and is visible in the universe, all creatures of flesh shall lift up their heads fr[om their sleep] towards the splendour of the sun, and open their doors. While at evening time, when the sun sinks from the universe, all people from every place and even all beasts shall go in to their dark hiding places. The population of the entire universe shuts their doors and dark night overcomes them. They go inside and stay within the dark night in their hiding places.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal correspondential setup: a twofold solar pattern (rising/setting) presented as ‘mysteries’ within the cosmic order of the universe/mixture, without institutional address or citation.

paragraphs.core_text: Very great is this mystery revealed by the sun! For when the sun rises and [be]come[s] visible at the beginning of the day all people open their doors, and all of humanity and every creature emerges onto the ear[th] to destroy this Light Cross that is established i[n] silence.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic mechanism in correspondential form: the daily emergence of embodied life is interpreted as assault on the Light Cross (a cosmological entity/process), staying within the Manichaean system rather than pointing to contemporary institutions.

paragraphs.core_text: This pertains to the mystery of the First Man, because when he came out from the grea[t]ness he shone forth over all the children of darkness. At that mome[nt] all the children of darkness came forth from their storehouses, its powers and its armies, abandoning their caves and their black abyss. They destroyed the [outer] body of his five sons, who were swathed over hi[s b]o[dy, in t]hat first struggle.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmological narration keyed to a structural correspondence (‘this pertains to…’): First Man’s descent and the five sons in the first struggle—core mythic-cosmic teaching; no frame markers or exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, when the sun sinks from the universe and sets, and all people go in to their hiding places and houses and conceal themselves; this also pertains to the mystery of the end, as it presages the consummation of the universe. For, when all the light will be purified and redeemed i[n] the universe at the last, the collector of all things, the Last Statue, will gather in and sculpt it/self. It is the last hour of the day, the time when the Last Statue will go up to the aeo[n of] light. The enemy too, Death, will go in to bondage; to the prison of the souls of the de[ni]iers and blasphemers who loved the darkness. They will go in with it to bondage and the dark night overcomes th[em]; and thenceforth this name 'light' will not shine upon them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Closes the twofold correspondence with eschatological cosmology (purification, Last Statue, Death/prison). The mapping remains cosmos→cosmos (solar setting → consummation), without institutional/pastoral application.

paragraphs.core_text: Behold the two mysteries made visible daily in the sun, which is this splendrous light-giver.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief impersonal recapitulation of the two-mystery solar correspondence; still expository, not hortatory or framed as dialogue.

Direct audience address (‘my brothers and loved ones’), imperatives (‘Take trouble… preach…’), repentance/time-to-do-good language—application to community practice, consistent with late pastoral graft (also matches the chapter’s second-half drift).
Narrative reaction formula (‘When his disciples heard…’) serving as hagiographic/dialogue frame closure rather than cosmological teaching.
